## 🛠️ Project Updates

One hands-on update this week - I had great fun with this - and a couple of rather useful informational updates. I am also continuing the *Principles of Economics series*. What are you doing?

### VMs made simple and more

I have used virtual machines (VMs) for a long time and everyone's favourite hypervisor is *VirtualBox -* even though it is owned by Oracle Corp and not fully open source but it is free. It can be rather quirky but once it works, it is OK. This week I discovered [*Gnome-Boxes*](https://apps.gnome.org/en-GB/Boxes/?ref=rogerprice.me). This is the right way to build a hypervisor - you will be amazed at how simple it is and how well it works.

> [!image]
> [![Who knew! Superbly interesting and easier than you would have thought](https://storage.ghost.io/c/9c/2a/9c2aa86d-156e-419f-9a0f-38bf91aebf15/content/images/2026/06/image-30.png)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1eaJJXZCQYU&ref=rogerprice.me)
> Who knew! Superbly interesting and easier than you would have thought

In this video Madhu demonstrates how you can set this up and get going in seconds. What are you waiting for?

For those who need a little more configuration possibilities, your choice will be [virt-manager](https://virt-manager.org/index.html?ref=rogerprice.me). This is file-compatible, allowing the same VM that you created in Boxes to be imported and run in virt-manager with whatever additional controls you need. This is next level stuff and truly fascinating.

### DMS and Niri

One of the immediate benefits is that you can easily and safely test out other distributions and desktop environments. For example, you might consider using a *Tiling Window manager* instead of the usual floating manager that you get by default everywhere. These can help you to focus with much less distractions.

> [!image]
> [![Click as Madhu demonstrates how easy this can be](https://storage.ghost.io/c/9c/2a/9c2aa86d-156e-419f-9a0f-38bf91aebf15/content/images/2026/06/image-31.png)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1FCAXMIVglU&ref=rogerprice.me)
> Click as Madhu demonstrates how easy this can be

### Browser wars are still ongoing

This week I came across this excellent summary of Brave Browser, how it came about and why more than 115 million people use it daily as their browser of choice. Once you understand this, you will likely join that number.

> [!image]
> [![Click to be surprised](https://storage.ghost.io/c/9c/2a/9c2aa86d-156e-419f-9a0f-38bf91aebf15/content/images/2026/06/image-24.png)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S-J4qeG9YdM&ref=rogerprice.me)
> Click to be surprised

Brave has long been the browser that I recommend people to pick and it remains a solid choice. However if you are a power user with many concurrent open tabs you will find that it is something of a memory hog.

Related to the above, this next one is a fascinating explainer by Foci. You may recall that for the last 6 months or so he has been going *full-tilt* into using Open Source, non-Big-Tech software on Linux for all his daily tasks. There are a few areas where this has proven harder than others but his progress and weekly reports are outstanding.

> [!image]
> [![Click for the update](https://storage.ghost.io/c/9c/2a/9c2aa86d-156e-419f-9a0f-38bf91aebf15/content/images/2026/06/image-25.png)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TGoVjilLT7Q&ref=rogerprice.me)
> Click for the update

TLDR - with this one he pushed me to take another look at my browser usage. Obviously I avoid Chrome, Micro$lop Edge and Apple's Safari. On Mac, Orion from Kagi is an interesting option; it does not meet all my needs and, like many, I have noticed that Brave does seem to be increasingly bloated in recent months. Foci has inspired me to give Zen and Helium a closer look - I'll be reporting back in due course. What is your preference and why?

BTW - I already have one interesting finding in favour of Zen Browser. In recent days Brave has been stuttering to start playing YouTube videos. It is solvable by reloading the page but it is rather annoying. Zen Browser with uBlockOrigin installed works perfectly and still no sign of any adverts. I recommend that you keep a few favourite browsers working and configured at all times - you may use each for specific purposes. Big Tech is getting increasingly invasive with its tracking and control; such diversity helps you keep your own privacy and control.

### Nicole says it like it is

After a century of rising intelligence (the **Flynn effect**), developed countries are now seeing declining literacy, numeracy, and IQ scores. Gen Z is the first generation in modern history to score lower on standardized tests than their parents. Nicole argues this isn't a genetic decline but a systemic one - modern society increasingly discourages the development of cognitive skills - this is an orchestrated failure.
